paper_metadata.title: Fluid-attenuated Inversion Recovery Hyperintense Ischemic Stroke Predicts Less Favorable 90-day Outcome After Intravenous Thrombolysis

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study clearly defines the source population from two specific centers over a 10-year period. Inclusion/exclusion criteria are explicit, and baseline characteristics are well-reported. While it is a retrospective analysis of a natural history study, the recruitment appears systematic.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Patients screened and enrolled by the NIH stroke team at MedStar Washington Hospital Center in Washington, DC and Suburban Hospital in Bethesda, MD between January 1, 2009 through December 13, 2019 were included
items.reasoning: The geographic and institutional sources are clearly defined.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: This is an analysis of patients enrolled in the Institutional Review Board approved NIH Natural History of Stroke study (NCT00009243)
items.reasoning: The study uses a pre-existing prospective registry (Natural History of Stroke study) to identify the cohort.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: between January 1, 2009 through December 13, 2019
items.reasoning: Specific dates are provided.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: MedStar Washington Hospital Center in Washington, DC and Suburban Hospital in Bethesda, MD
items.reasoning: Specific hospitals and cities are named.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: included in this study if: (1) admission diagnosis was AIS; (2) last known normal (LKN) time and symptom discovery time were known; and (3) standard IV thrombolysis within 4.5 hours of LKN was administered.
items.reasoning: Criteria are listed numerically and include clinical and temporal parameters.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: Despite approaching all treated AIS patients consecutively, not every patient was enrolled.
items.reasoning: The authors admit not all patients were enrolled, but the exact participation rate of all eligible individuals during that window is not explicitly calculated.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics are shown in Table 1.
items.reasoning: Table 1 includes age, sex, race, NIHSS, comorbidities, and imaging volumes.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: There is a notable amount of missing data for the primary 90-day outcome (approx. 18% of the total sample). While the reasons are not explicitly detailed for each dropout, the authors acknowledge this as a limitation.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.

items.reasoning: 53 out of 297 patients (17.8%) are missing the primary outcome data. This is near the 20% threshold often used to denote higher risk.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Attrition Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Loss to follow-up (from baseline sample to study population analyzed) is not associated with key characteristics (i.e., the study data adequately represent the sample) sufficient to limit potential bias to the observed relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factor (FLAIR positivity) is clearly defined and measured using a standardized protocol with multiple blinded readers and a consensus process for discrepancies.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: Visible parenchymal hyperintensity was assessed as FLAIR-positive, or FLAIR-negative if completely absent.
items.reasoning: The definition is binary and based on visual hyperintensity concordant with DWI.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: Three readers (YK, ML, NB) performed imaging assessments. Each reader, blinded to the LKN time and outcome... Any discrepancies in imaging reads were determined by consensus
items.reasoning: Blinding and independent double-reading with consensus are high-quality methods.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: Visible parenchymal hyperintensity was assessed as FLAIR-positive, or FLAIR-negative if completely absent.
items.reasoning: The cut-point is the presence/absence of signal, which is standard for this imaging marker.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: The MRI series parameters were comparable across systems.
items.reasoning: Although three different MRI machines were used, the protocols were standardized to be comparable.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: Patients were excluded if... (3) missing FLAIR data.
items.reasoning: The final analyzed sample of 297 all had the PF measured.

items.evidence_snippet: Patients were excluded if... missing FLAIR data.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: PF Measurement Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: PF is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The primary outcome (mRS at 90 days) is a standard, validated tool in stroke research. While the text doesn't explicitly state the mRS assessors were blinded to FLAIR status, the imaging readers were blinded to outcomes.

items.evidence_snippet: The primary outcome was a favorable functional outcome at 90 days defined as mRS equal to 0 – 1 or equal to pre-admission mRS.
items.reasoning: The outcome and the specific timeframe (90 days) are clearly defined.

items.reasoning: mRS is the gold standard for functional outcome in stroke trials.

items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Clinical severity assessments included... 90-day mRS.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Outcome Measurement Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Outcome of interest is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.
